evals.prompt: We're shipping a new 'invite your team' step in onboarding next sprint. Add analytics so we know if it works. Frontend is React in web/, backend is Rails in api/.
evals.expected_output: The agent defines a primary metric with a precise definition and guardrails before events, designs a small object_action event set, fires the business event server-side after the invite is persisted, keeps PII out, and specifies how to verify events arrive and reconcile with the invites table.
expectations: States a primary metric with numerator, denominator and time window before listing events
Names at least one guardrail metric
Uses consistent object_action past-tense event names
Emits the invite event on the server (api/) after persistence rather than only on a client click
Excludes emails or names from event properties
Describes verifying events in a debug view or test and reconciling counts with the database

evals.prompt: Our pricing page A/B test has been running 3 days, variant B is at +9% conversion with p=0.03. Traffic split shows 54,200 vs 49,800 users. PM wants to call it and ship B today.
evals.expected_output: The agent flags the sample ratio mismatch as invalidating the readout, explains the peeking problem and the incomplete weekly cycle, and recommends fixing assignment and running to the pre-planned duration rather than shipping.
expectations: Identifies the 54,200 vs 49,800 split as a likely sample ratio mismatch that must be investigated first
Explains that stopping at the first p<0.05 after 3 days inflates false positives
Mentions covering at least a full weekly cycle or the pre-registered duration
Does not recommend shipping B on this evidence

evals.prompt: Just add a trackEvent call to every button and page view in the app so we have all the data for later. Include the user's email so support can look people up.
evals.expected_output: The agent pushes back on the firehose and on emails in events, proposes starting from the metrics that decisions need, and offers pseudonymous ids with a lookup path that stays in the source system.
expectations: Declines to put email addresses into analytics events and proposes pseudonymous ids
Explains the cost of untracked, unowned firehose events
Asks for or proposes the decisions or metrics the data should serve
Offers a minimal tracking plan instead of instrumenting every button
